note: AJAX Comments has a global config object ajax_comments.settings (booleans notify [default true], enable_scroll [default true], reply_autoclose [default false]) at route ajax_comments.settings (admin/config/content/ajax_comments), plus a per-comment-field third-party setting third_party_settings.ajax_comments.enable_ajax_comments (default '1') on the comment field's display component. Medium cases change ONE global setting from its default and ask the agent to identify which one differs (discoverable, grades on the setting name); hard cases set a known baseline and verify exact boolean values via drush cget. Cleanup restores shipped defaults (notify=true, enable_scroll=true, reply_autoclose=false).

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the AJAX Comments module, what is the config object for its global settings, at what admin path is the settings form, and what are the three options it offers?
evals.expected_output: Config object ajax_comments.settings at admin/config/content/ajax_comments (route ajax_comments.settings). Options: notify (message after posting), enable_scroll (scroll to the comment), reply_autoclose (auto-close other open reply forms).

evals.prompt: With AJAX Comments installed, how do I turn AJAX behavior on or off for a specific comment field, and is it on by default?
evals.expected_output: It is enabled by default (the third-party setting enable_ajax_comments defaults to '1'). Toggle it on the comment field's display settings; it is stored as third_party_settings.ajax_comments.enable_ajax_comments on the comment field's formatter component in the entity_view_display.

evals.prompt: What core module does AJAX Comments depend on, and does it define its own permissions for who can post/edit comments via AJAX?
evals.expected_output: It depends on the core Comment module. It defines no permissions of its own; access to the AJAX add/reply/edit/delete endpoints is governed by core comment entity access (post comments, edit own comments, administer comments, etc.).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one of AJAX Comments' three global settings has been changed from its shipped default. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which setting differs and its current value.
evals.expected_output: reply_autoclose has been set to true (its shipped default is false); notify and enable_scroll are still true. Read with: drush cget ajax_comments.settings.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, AJAX Comments has been configured to NOT do one thing it does by default. Inspect the live ajax_comments configuration and name the setting that has been turned off.
evals.expected_output: notify has been set to false (default true), so no status message is shown after posting a comment via AJAX. Read with: drush cget ajax_comments.settings notify.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure AJAX Comments so that opening a reply form automatically closes any other open reply form, and so that NO notification message is shown after a comment is posted. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In ajax_comments.settings set reply_autoclose to true and notify to false (via the settings form or configFactory getEditable set save).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, AJAX Comments currently scrolls the page to the affected comment after each AJAX action. Turn that scrolling behavior off. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In ajax_comments.settings set enable_scroll to false.
